title: Censorship
intro: What government officials did about Americans' speech on social media, as shown by court records, official transcripts, company letters and subpoenaed documents; what the courts actually held; and what is popularly believed but not supported by the record.

sections.title: Popularly believed but not supported by the record
notes: Each belief is shown with what the primary record does and does not show.
Not supported by the record The FBI or the government ordered the laptop story suppressed.

Yoel Roth testified under oath that Hunter Biden was raised in FBI meetings “but not by the government, to the best of my recollection.” Matt Taibbi wrote: “no evidence - that I've seen - of any government involvement in the laptop story.” What is documented: general FBI hack-and-leak warnings and the FBI declining to comment when asked. The district court called that “significant encouragement” (p. 107); the finding was preliminary and later vacated.
Not supported by the record The Twitter Files show the Biden White House ordering takedowns in 2020.

In 2020 the “Biden team” was a campaign. Twitter Files #1: requests from “both the Trump White House and the Biden campaign were received and honored.” The “Handled” email was dated Oct 24, 2020, after the laptop decision.
Twitter Files #1
Not supported by the record The Supreme Court cleared the administration and found no censorship.
The Court decided standing only: “We therefore lack jurisdiction to reach the merits.” It made no finding that pressure did not occur.
Murthy v. Missouri
Not supported by the record The courts ruled the administration's actions unconstitutional.
The district and Fifth Circuit findings were preliminary (“likely”) and were vacated on Aug 26, 2024. The 2026 consent decree is not an admission of liability.
Not supported by the record Francis Collins and Anthony Fauci got the Great Barrington Declaration censored.
Collins's FOIA-released email asks for “a quick and devastating published take down of its premises,” which means a published rebuttal, not removal. The Fifth Circuit found NIAID not liable.
Not supported by the record Doctors lost their licenses just for speaking.

Washington's order on Dr. Ryan Cole restricted his license, citing both his statements and deficient care for four patients. California's AB 2098 was enjoined on vagueness grounds, then repealed by SB 815; no enforcement was found. The FSMB warned in 2021 that spreading vaccine misinformation risked discipline. No primary record reviewed shows a revocation for speech alone.
Not supported by the record Networks censored the President on Nov 5, 2020.
The full address was carried unedited by C-SPAN and the White House, and the official transcript exists. Any cutaways were decisions by private broadcasters; no government actor was involved.
Not supported by the record The Hunter Biden laptop story was Russian disinformation.

Candidate Biden cited a letter from 51 former intelligence officials, which said the emails had “all the classic earmarks of a Russian information operation”. Zuckerberg later wrote that “the reporting was not Russian disinformation.”

sections.title: What happened to the physician plaintiffs

censorship-1.title: White House digital director Rob Flaherty to Twitter, Feb 6, 2021
lines: “Cannot stress the degree to which this needs to be resolved immediately.”

About a parody account of President Biden's granddaughter; Twitter suspended it within about 45 minutes (district court ruling, p. 9). The Supreme Court later noted (fn. 4) that this impersonation request was mischaracterized as a censorship request.
W.D. La. ruling, ECF 293 Murthy v. Missouri

censorship-2.title: Rob Flaherty to Facebook, Jul 15, 2021
lines: “Are you guys f***ing serious? I want an answer on what happened here and I want it today.”
Quoted in the district court's findings (p. 23). The profanity is shown with letters masked; the court record prints the word in full.

censorship-3.title: Press Secretary Jen Psaki, Jul 15–16, 2021
lines: “We're flagging problematic posts for Facebook … there's about 12 people who are producing 65 percent of anti-vaccine misinformation.”

The next day: “we're in regular touch with social media platforms … You all make decisions, just like the social media platforms make decisions,” and “You shouldn't be banned from one platform and not others.”
Briefing transcript, Jul 15 Briefing transcript, Jul 16

censorship-4.title: Surgeon General's advisory, Jul 15, 2021
lines: “Impose clear consequences for accounts that repeatedly violate platform policies.”

It also urged platforms to “prioritize early detection of misinformation ‘super-spreaders’ and repeat offenders.” Its definition of misinformation covers a true anecdote that is “highly misleading,” and it warns against “conflating controversial or unorthodox claims with misinformation.”

censorship-5.title: President Biden, Jul 16 and 19, 2021
lines: “They're killing people.”
Three days later: “Facebook isn't killing people; these 12 people who are out there giving misinformation—anyone listening to it is getting hurt by it. It's killing people.”
PBS raw video Official transcript, Jul 19

censorship-6.title: CDC "COVID BOLO" meetings with platforms, from May 14, 2021
lines: CDC's Carol Crawford set up “Be On the Lookout” meetings with platforms; Census Bureau staff helped prepare the slides (district court ruling, p. 47). The Fifth Circuit found CDC “not plainly coercive” but “likely significantly encouraged” platform decisions (vacated later).
W.D. La. ruling, p. 47 5th Cir., Sep 8, 2023

censorship-7.title: CISA "switchboarding"
lines: CISA forwarded election officials' flags to platforms, which decided under their own policies; the practice stopped in 2022 (district court ruling, p. 68, citing CISA's Brian Scully). The House Judiciary majority staff calls it censorship; that is the committee majority's characterization.
W.D. La. ruling, p. 68 House Judiciary majority-staff report

censorship-8.title: Mark Zuckerberg to Chairman Jordan, Aug 26, 2024
lines: “In 2021, senior officials from the Biden Administration, including the White House, repeatedly pressured our teams for months to censor certain COVID-19 content, including humor and satire, and expressed a lot of frustration with our teams when we didn't agree.”

Also: “I believe the government pressure was wrong” and “Ultimately, it was our decision whether or not to take content down, and we own our decisions.” On the laptop story he describes a general FBI warning, not one naming the Post story, and says “in retrospect, we shouldn't have demoted the story.”

censorship-9.title: Alphabet (YouTube) to Chairman Jordan, Sep 23, 2025
lines: “pressed the Company regarding certain user-generated content … that did not violate its policies.”

¶10: “It is unacceptable and wrong when any government … attempts to dictate how the Company moderates content.” ¶23: creators terminated under its COVID and election policies will be offered a way back. Counterpoint on the record: Ranking Member Raskin's Oct 30, 2025 letter says “not a single one of Alphabet's employees testified about any coercion.” Both companies say the final decisions were their own.
Alphabet letter Raskin letter (minority)

censorship-10.title: Facebook staff to Nick Clegg, Jul 14, 2021: "under pressure"
lines: “Because we were under pressure from the administration and others to do more … We shouldn't have done it.”

The answer to why Facebook had removed claims that COVID was man-made. Subpoenaed company email, reproduced in the House Judiciary majority report (pp. 13–14, Ex. 52). Facebook's own policy page shows it removed “man-made” claims from Feb 8, 2021 and stopped on May 26, 2021. Official intelligence assessments of COVID's origin remain split; the 2021 ODNI assessment calls both origins “plausible.”
House Judiciary report Appendix of documents Facebook policy page ODNI 2021

censorship-11.title: Stanford-led Election Integrity Partnership and Virality Project
lines: “35% of the URLs we shared with Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, and YouTube were either labeled, removed, or soft blocked.”

The EIP was formed “in consultation with CISA” (639 in-scope tickets; 72% about delegitimizing the election; 16% filed by the nonprofit Center for Internet Security). The Virality Project (911 tickets) reports “strong ties” with the Surgeon General's office and CDC, says the Surgeon General's office “incorporated VP's research and perspectives,” and says platforms acted “in accordance with their policies.” A Virality Project email told Twitter that “true stories that could fuel hesitancy” should be treated as “Standard Vaccine Misinformation on Your Platform” (Twitter Files #19 screenshot).
EIP, The Long Fuse Virality Project report Twitter Files #19 screenshot

censorship-12.title: Trump account suspensions, in the companies' own words
lines: Twitter (Jan 8, 2021) cited “the risk of further incitement of violence”; Twitter Files #5 shows staff had earlier written “I think we'd have a hard time saying this is incitement.” The Oversight Board (May 5, 2021) upheld Facebook's restriction but called an indefinite suspension “indeterminate and standardless”; Facebook set two years (Jun 4, 2021) and reinstated him Jan 25, 2023. YouTube settled his suit for $24.5M (ECF 178, Sep 29, 2025).
Twitter post (court exhibit) Twitter Files #5 Oversight Board Meta reinstatement YouTube settlement, ECF 178

censorship-13.title: W.D. La. (Judge Doughty)
lines: Date: Jul 4, 2023
What it held: Preliminary injunction granted in part. Plaintiffs “likely” to succeed. The “most massive attack against free speech” line opens with “If the allegations made by Plaintiffs are true.”
Status: Preliminary; later vacated
censorship-13.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-14.title: Fifth Circuit
lines: Date: Sep 8 and Oct 3, 2023
What it held: White House, Surgeon General, FBI, CDC and (on rehearing) CISA “likely coerced or significantly encouraged” platform decisions. NIAID and the State Department not liable.
Status: Preliminary; later vacated
censorship-14.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-15.title: U.S. Supreme Court (Barrett, 6–3)
lines: Date: Jun 26, 2024

What it held: Reversed on standing only: “We therefore lack jurisdiction to reach the merits.” Footnote 4: many district findings “unfortunately appear to be clearly erroneous.” Alito's dissent (with Thomas and Gorsuch) called the conduct “blatantly unconstitutional”; a dissent is not a holding.
Status: Final on standing; no merits ruling
censorship-15.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-16.title: Fifth Circuit on remand
lines: Date: Aug 26, 2024
What it held: Injunction vacated entirely; case remanded.
Status: Everything preliminary wiped
censorship-16.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-17.title: W.D. La.
lines: Date: Nov 8, 2024
What it held: Jurisdictional discovery allowed.
Status: Procedural
censorship-17.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-18.title: W.D. La. consent decree
lines: Date: Mar 25, 2026

What it held: SO ORDERED: for 10 years the Surgeon General, CDC and CISA may not threaten “adverse legal, regulatory, or economic government sanction” to get the plaintiffs' protected speech removed from Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn or YouTube. Officials may still call posts “inaccurate, wrong.” ¶17: not an admission of liability.
Status: Settlement; not a finding
censorship-18.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-19.title: Bottom line
lines: No court has issued a final ruling that any official violated the First Amendment in this matter. The case ended in a limited consent decree that expressly is not an admission of liability.
censorship-19.label: Verified by SwampForce

censorship-20.title: Characterizations, not findings
lines: House Judiciary majority-staff reports use words such as “unconstitutional” and “colluded”; these are the committee majority's conclusions. Majority report
Executive Order 14149 (Jan 20, 2025) says the prior administration “trampled free speech rights”; that is the executive's characterization, not a court finding. EO 14149
At the Mar 9, 2023 Weaponization hearing, Taibbi named requests from the FBI, DHS, HHS, DOD, GEC and CIA; these are witness claims in a congressional record. Hearing record

censorship-27.title: Dr. Jay Bhattacharya (co-author of the Great Barrington Declaration)
lines: Twitter placed him on a “Trends Blacklist” (Twitter Files #2; the screenshots show no government request behind it). Confirmed NIH Director on Mar 25, 2025, 53–47. Twitter Files #2 Senate roll call #141

censorship-28.title: Dr. Martin Kulldorff
lines: a tweet labeled “Misleading” by Twitter (Twitter Files #10). Chaired the CDC vaccine advisory committee (ACIP) in 2025; named chief science officer at HHS ASPE on Dec 1, 2025. Per plaintiffs' counsel, he and Bhattacharya withdrew from the case on joining government. Twitter Files #10 HHS release
